title: Lightator: An Optical Near-Sensor Accelerator with Compressive Acquisition Enabling Versatile Image Processing
problem: Vision applications suffer from high energy consumption and latency due to data conversion, transmission, and processing in cloud-centric and edge accelerator architectures.
motivation: Photonic devices offer superior energy efficiency compared to electronic systems for processing vision workloads at the edge.
method: Lightator processes images right at the camera sensor using light-based devices, before data leaves the hardware. First, it compresses the raw image data at the sensor (keeping only essential information to reduce volume), then it performs the core image-processing math—convolutions—using light instead of electricity. This near-sensor, light-based approach eliminates two expensive steps: converting signals between light and electricity, and transmitting data to a distant processor.
key_novelty: Combining compressed image acquisition and fine-grained optical convolutions at the camera sensor in one light-based device, eliminating the need to send data to the cloud for processing.
contributions: Novel optical near-sensor accelerator (Lightator) implementing compressive acquisition capability
Fine-grained convolution operations executed on photonic hardware
Achieves 84.4 Kilo FPS/W with 24× power reduction vs photonic accelerators and 73× vs GPU baseline
Enables versatile image processing at the edge with reduced latency and energy consumption
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; specific accuracy trade-offs and deployment scalability limitations not detailed.
primary_theme: optical near-sensor accelerator for edge vision processing
